title: Taking the first hot chorus with a rap, and the closing thanks
summary: Vincent claims to be the first to take a hot chorus on banjo using a double rap, learned from Julius and perfected with a tin pan behind his banjo. The session ends with thanks.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, I asked him about, did anybody take a hot chorus and play chords? Or did they always pick it?

He said, did anybody take a hot chorus and play it with chords or pick, pick it? I was the first one that took that hot chorus. Was picking or? Wrapping. Wrapping. Yeah. Wrapping. You know, Eddie, not by myself, the whole band stopped. And just the kick-toe and the bass would take a hot. Oh yeah. But now, every man in the band takes a hot, you see. You see, I had a rap like that, you know. Oh yeah. Like that, you know. None of them couldn't catch that rap, but now they know it now, you see. I taught it over in Mexico. Made plenty of money off it. And these tick-toe players, band-toe players used to come around me and watch me. And I called it from another fellow named Julius. He tired. He had lung trouble too. And he used to play down on the front and the streets for two of them. And sometimes them brothers used to come and say, Dad, why don't you play and make that rap, double rap like Julius? I said, I can't. I said, why don't you blow that hole and go away up there like Julius? I'm strong. He said, I can't. Well, I said, I can't do it either. And then when I did get that thing, I got one of my mother's old tin panes, you know, put it behind my banjo. And it sounds so good. And I just kept on sitting down there and I got it. And I got it. And I couldn't stop. I said, oh, Mom, I got it. I got my sister. I said, I have to laugh. And then when I come out, and friends with musicians come around me like that. And they let us laugh. And who join Academy to make me do it all the time.
He told me he liked that today. Yeah.
